pages.x: RMS Titanic, built in Belfast for the White Star Line, was the largest ship in the world, 269 metres long, with a gym, a swimming pool and a grand staircase under a glass dome. Her hull was split into compartments that could be sealed off, and people called her unsinkable. She carried lifeboats for only about half of those on board.

On 10 April 1912 she sailed from Southampton for New York with some 2,200 people aboard, from millionaires like John Jacob Astor to emigrants in third class from Ireland, Scandinavia and Lebanon, hoping for a new life in America.

Other ships had radioed warnings of ice, but the Titanic kept up her speed through a calm, moonless night. At 11:40 pm on 14 April a lookout saw an iceberg dead ahead. The ship swung but scraped along it, and the sea poured into her front compartments. Her designer, on board, told the captain she would sink within hours.

The crew loaded the lifeboats, women and children first, but many left half empty because people would not believe the ship could sink. The band played on deck to keep everyone calm. At 2:20 am the Titanic broke in two and went down, leaving hundreds in the freezing water.

The liner Carpathia, racing through the ice, picked up the survivors at dawn. More than half of the first-class passengers lived, but only a quarter of those in third class, many trapped in the maze of corridors below. Most of the crew died, among them the captain, the designer and the whole band.
The first international treaty for the safety of life at sea, agreed in London in 1914.
pages.fx: Ships had to carry lifeboats for everyone on board and keep a radio watch day and night, and an International Ice Patrol began watching for icebergs in the North Atlantic. It still does.

pages.x: In 1985 a team led by the ocean explorer Robert Ballard found the wreck almost four kilometres down, lying in two pieces on the sea floor. Expeditions have filmed it many times since, and its story has been told in books, songs and films.
The Titanic became a lasting symbol of human pride humbled by nature, and of a society split by class even at the moment of death. Its loss brought in the first international rules for safety at sea.
